text:
Hana Kim: Hi all, quick onboarding questions. I enrolled in the HDHP + HSA but my benefits summary still shows $0 contributions. Also I added my newborn as dependent and uploaded the birth certificate, but my pay stub shows no change to premiums. Who should I ping?

Ava (People Ops): Welcome Hana! Congrats on the baby. HSA contributions and dependent additions often require carrier + payroll sync. Sanya handles benefits carrier side and Liam does payroll.

Sanya (Benefits): Looking now. I see your HSA election marked Complete on 07/02 but the HSA custodian batch went out after payroll cutoff. You should see contributions begin on the 07/15 pay run. For the newborn, I see a Pending enrollment because the uploaded birth cert was missing the hospital stamp. Can you re-upload a stamped copy or a physician's letter?

Hana Kim: Uploaded a new PDF as "Kim_Hana_newborn_birth_07012024_stamped.pdf" just now.

BenefitsBot: Document received and queued (position 2). Expected processing within 24 hours.

Sanya (Benefits): Got it, I'll manually approve once it appears. If approved today, newborn coverage effective date will be 07/01 and payroll will pick up premium change on 07/15.

Hana Kim: Thanks. One more thing  my paycheck preview shows a line "Pre-tax commuter: 0.00" but I did enroll in commuter. Should that be $100?

Liam (Payroll): Hi Hana, commuter elections sometimes don't hit payroll until after the first successful bank file for pre-tax elections. Did you enroll before 07/01 cutoff?

Hana Kim: I enrolled on 07/02 so probably missed the cutoff. Will it appear on 07/15 then?

Liam (Payroll): Yes, commuter will appear on 07/15. If it doesn't, DM me and I'll check the import logs. Also note: newborn premium retro adjustments, if any, may appear as a separate deduction to collect premiums back to 07/01. We try to smooth deductions when possible.

Hana Kim: OK good to know. One last quick tax question: I changed my W-4 to claim 0 and extra $50 withholding. Does that change show up immediately or on next payroll?

Liam (Payroll): W-4 changes entered in Workday before the payroll cutoff apply to the next run. If you changed it after the cutoff it will apply to 07/15. I see your change effective 07/03 so it will apply on 07/15.

Hana Kim: Thank you all! Appreciate the quick responses.

Ava (People Ops): Summary: Sanya to approve newborn once document processes (effect 07/01) -> payroll picks premium + HSA + commuter on 07/15; W-4 change effective 07/15. Ping benefits@redwood.com or payroll@redwood.com for follow-ups.
